walkthroughs.title: Perkins Builder Brothers Ep.4 (6 mil)
walkthroughs.what_it_shows: Spoken 6 mil, laps a couple feet. Field 2-story. Book hold is 12-in laps — confirm AHJ, do not invent a winner from “a couple feet.”
flags: laps a couple feet — book is 12-in

labor.named_not_headcount: ORNL checklist names construction contractor; AF&PA names job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector — not a headcount

remodel_note: Remodel extras not in these books — Gap, do not invent.
habit_scope: 6-mil polyethylene under basement slab and SOG, before the pour. Poly 12-in laps already named on P05; this Method is the underslab sequence. 1–2 story wood SFR / ADU.
how_it_is_done: Compact fill under slab (ORNL FLOOR SLAB). Then a minimum 4-inch-thick layer of coarse, clean gravel under the slab (ORNL RADON CONTROL MEASURES / FLOOR SLAB). HUD §4.6: 2–3 in washed gravel or sand + 6-mil poly; gravel is the capillary break.
Lay 6-mil (minimum) polyethylene on top of the gravel (ORNL radon sealing the floor; Ch 4 slab). Film is a radon and moisture retarder and keeps concrete out of the aggregate as it is cast.

Lap edges at least 12 inches (ORNL Ch 2 radon; Ch 4 slab). Extend poly over the top of the footing / sealed to the foundation wall, or over the top of the foundation wall, or to the outer bottom edge of a monolithic slab-grade beam (ORNL Ch 2 / Ch 4).
Slit an 'x' at penetrations; turn up the tabs and tape them. Do not puncture; consider rounded riverbed gravel (ORNL Ch 2 / Ch 4).
Optional 2-inch sand layer on top of the polyethylene improves curing and puncture protection. Dampen the sand, do not saturate, before the pour (ORNL Ch 4).

Locate plumbing, electrical service, and gas service to be cast in the slab (ORNL slab checklist). Caulk joints around pipes and conduits (ORNL RADON CONTROL MEASURES). Form a gap of at least 1/2 inch around plumbing/utility lead-ins through the slab to a depth of at least 1/2 inch; fill with polyurethane or similar (ORNL Ch 2 sealing the basement floor item 9).
Remove all grade stakes, spreader sticks, and wood embedded in concrete during the pour (ORNL RADON / TERMITE checklists). That is a pour-day hold, shared with P05.
12-in laps and 6-mil class are already on P05 methods. This Method does not change the class — it times the placement before the pour (P06).
trades: construction contractor — named, not a headcount
tools_equipment: Not a tool list. Named: poly placement; tape at penetration tabs.
inspection_hold_points: Vapor retarder in place under slab; 6-mil; 12-in laps (ORNL; HUD §4.6).
Poly sealed to wall / over footing / over top of foundation wall / to outer bottom edge of monolithic grade beam (ORNL Ch 2 / Ch 4).
4-in coarse clean gravel under the slab (ORNL).
Fill compacted under slab (ORNL FLOOR SLAB).
Plumbing/electrical/gas located before the pour (ORNL slab checklist).
Grade stakes / spreader sticks / wood out of the pour (ORNL).
inspector_looks_for: 6-mil poly down, 12-in laps, sealed to wall or over footing (ORNL).
Gravel bed under the poly (ORNL 4-in coarse clean).
No wood left in the pour (ORNL).
common_messups: Puncturing the poly on sharp gravel (ORNL: consider riverbed gravel).
Leaving grade stakes / spreader sticks in the slab (ORNL).
Saturating the optional sand layer before the pour (ORNL: dampen, do not saturate).
smart_save: Gap — book did not name a dollar save on poly. Riverbed gravel is named as a puncture/soil-gas path, not a cheap skip.
do_not_cheap: 4-in coarse clean gravel under the slab (ORNL).
Poly sealed to the wall / over the footing (ORNL).
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit under basement slabs and SOG. Not an alt.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Skipping poly because P05 already named the class — the class still has to be on the dirt before the pour. Skipping laps.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — plastic under the slab. What they skip is 12-in laps, sealing to the wall, and getting the stakes out.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Vapor retarder / gravel under slab on the drawings. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
risk_if_swapped_late: You cannot add 12-in laps after the pour. Catch before the truck.
plain_language_summary: Before the slab truck, compact the fill, put down at least 4 inches of clean gravel, then 6-mil plastic with 12-inch laps, sealed to the wall. Cut an X at pipes and tape the tabs. Optional 2 inches of damp sand on the plastic so it does not puncture. Get the wood stakes out. The plastic class is the same one P05 already named — this is when it goes down.
spanish_summary: Antes del camión de losa, compacte, ponga al menos 4 pulgadas de grava limpia, luego plástico 6 mil con traslapes de 12 pulgadas, sellado a la pared. X en los tubos y tape las pestañas. Arena húmeda opcional de 2 pulgadas para no pinchar. Estacas de madera fuera. La clase de plástico ya está en P05 — aquí es cuándo se pone.
locators: ORNL BFH Ch 2 RADON CONTROL TECHNIQUES: 6-mil poly, 12-in laps, sealed to wall / over footing; 2-in sand optional
ORNL BFH Ch 4 RADON CONTROL TECHNIQUES: 6-mil on gravel; 12-in laps; extend over top of foundation wall or to outer bottom edge of monolithic grade beam
ORNL FLOOR SLAB / RADON CONTROL MEASURES: vapor retarder under slab; compact fill; 4-in gravel; locate plumbing/electrical/gas; remove grade stakes
HUD RSDG §4.6: 2–3 in washed gravel or sand + 6-mil poly
confidence_notes: 6-mil + 12-in laps printed in ORNL Ch 2 and Ch 4. HUD 2–3 in gravel vs ORNL 4-in radon gravel — do not pick a winner; follow the radon/underslab path when radon is in play (4-in) and HUD §4.6 2–3 in as capillary-break habit. Confirm with AHJ.
layering: Compact fill → gravel (4-in coarse clean for radon path / HUD 2–3 in capillary) → 6-mil poly 12-in laps sealed to wall → optional 2-in damp sand → pour.
1/2 in gap around slab penetrations filled with polyurethane (ORNL Ch 2 item 9).
code_to_check: Adopted vapor-retarder / under-slab gravel thickness at the AHJ. HUD §4.6 prints 2–3 in; ORNL radon path prints 4-in coarse clean. Do not pick a winner. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
time_money: Gap — no dollars. Completing poly before the pour is the book sequence, not a named save.
